risk_if_not_implemented: Without Third-Party Access Revocation, former third-party personnel and systems may retain physical and logical access after the relationship ends, creating unauthorized access paths that are easy to overlook. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege (R-AC-2), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Revocation of Access Authorizations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to revoke logical and physical access authorizations.
compensating_control_1.justification: Revocation of Access Authorizations (IAC-29) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Access Revocation (TPM-24.4) by revoking access authorizations when the conditions that justified them no longer exist, which removes third-party access through the organization's standard revocation process. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Periodic Review of Individual & Service Account Privileges
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically-review the privileges assigned to individuals and service accounts to validate the need for such privileges and reassign or remove unnecessary privileges, as necessary.
compensating_control_2.justification: Periodic Review of Individual & Service Account Privileges (IAC-12) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Access Revocation (TPM-24.4) by periodically reviewing individual and service account privileges, which detects and removes third-party access that was not revoked at cessation. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
